units.zh: 《南齊書》，八紀，十一志，四十列傳，合五十九篇，梁蕭子顯撰。
units.en: The 《Book of Southern Qi》 comprises eight annals, eleven treatises, and forty biographies—fifty-nine fascicles in all—written by Xiao Zixian of the Liang dynasty.
units.literal: The 《Book of Southern Qi》: eight annals, eleven treatises, forty biographies, fifty-nine fascicles in all, compiled by Xiao Zixian of Liang.

units.zh: 始江淹已爲十志，沈約又爲《齊紀》，而子顯自表武帝，別爲此書。
units.en: Jiang Yan had already drafted ten treatises, and Shen Yue had also written the 《Qi Chronicle》; but Zixian, having presented himself to Emperor Wu of Liang, undertook this work as a separate history.
units.literal: At first Jiang Yan had already composed ten treatises, and Shen Yue had also written the 《Qi Chronicle》, but Zixian, having himself petitioned Emperor Wu, separately produced this book.

units.zh: 臣等因校正其訛謬，而敘其篇目，曰：
units.en: We, your subjects, have corrected its errors and set forth the table of contents, saying:
units.literal: We, your subjects, therefore corrected its errors and blunders, and set forth its table of contents, saying:

units.zh: 將以是非得失、興壞理亂之故而爲法戒，則必得其所託，而後能傳於久，此史之所以作也。
units.en: When history is meant to serve as warning and model from the rights and wrongs, gains and losses, rise and ruin, and order and chaos of the past, it must find the right historian to carry it; only then can it endure. That is why histories are written.
units.literal: When one intends to take right and wrong, gain and loss, rise and ruin, order and chaos as models and warnings, one must secure the right person as one's medium, and only then can it be transmitted for long—this is why histories are written.

units.zh: 然而所託不得其人，則或失其意，或亂其實，或析理之不通，或設辭之不善，故雖有殊功韙德非常之迹，將闇而不章，鬱而不發，而檮杌嵬瑣姦回凶慝之形，可幸而掩也。
units.en: Yet if the historian is not the right person, the intent may be lost, the facts distorted, the reasoning muddled, or the style poor; then even extraordinary merit and towering virtue may lie hidden and never break into the light, while villains, petty scoundrels, traitors, and wicked men may by good fortune escape exposure.
units.literal: Yet when the medium is not the right person, then one may lose the intent, or corrupt the facts, or fail to reason through clearly, or compose ineffectively; thus even extraordinary merit and great virtue may grow obscure and fail to shine forth, while the shapes of taowu villains, base petty men, treacherous subversives, and vicious evildoers may fortunately be covered up.

units.zh: 嘗試論之，古之所謂良史者，其明必足以周萬事之理，其道必足以適天下之用，其智必足以通難知之意，其文必足以發難顯之情，然後其任可得而稱也。
units.en: Consider what the ancients meant by a fine historian: his clarity must encompass the principles of all things; his Way must meet the needs of the world; his wisdom must penetrate what is hard to know; his prose must express what is hard to make plain—only then can his work be said to have fulfilled its charge.
units.literal: I have tried to discuss this: what the ancients called a fine historian—his clarity must suffice to comprehend all principles of things, his Way must suffice to serve the needs of the world, his wisdom must suffice to penetrate what is hard to know, and his style must suffice to express what is hard to reveal; only then can his task be held to have been fulfilled.

units.zh: 何以知其然邪？
units.en: How do we know that this is so?
units.literal: How do we know this to be so?

units.zh: 昔者，唐虞有神明之性，有微妙之德，使由之者不能知，知之者不能名。
units.en: In antiquity Tang and Yu possessed a divine nature and subtle virtue: those who followed them could not fully grasp it, and those who grasped it could not put it into words.
units.literal: In former times, Tang and Yu possessed a divine nature and subtle virtue, such that those who followed them could not understand it, and those who understood could not name it.

units.zh: 以爲治天下之本，號令之所布，法度之所設，其言至約，其體至備，以爲冶天下之具。
units.en: They made this the foundation of governing the realm: in the commands they issued and the laws and institutions they established, their words were supremely spare and their forms supremely complete—the whole apparatus for ruling the world.
units.literal: They took this as the root of governing the world; in what they proclaimed as commands and established as laws and institutions, their words were supremely concise and their forms supremely complete—it was treated as the toolkit for governing the world.

units.zh: 而爲二《典》者，推而明之，所記者，豈獨其迹邪？
units.en: Those who composed the two 《Canons》 of Yao and Shun developed and clarified this: what they recorded—was it only their outward deeds?
units.literal: Yet those who composed the two 《Canons》 developed and clarified this: what they recorded—was it only their traces?

units.zh: 並與其深微之意而傳之。
units.en: They transmitted their profound and subtle intentions as well.
units.literal: They also transmitted along with them their profound and subtle intentions.

units.zh: 小大精粗，無不盡也；
units.en: Great and small, fine and coarse—nothing was left out;
units.literal: Whether great or small, fine or coarse, nothing was left incomplete;

units.zh: 本末先後，無不白也。
units.en: root and branch, earlier and later—nothing was left obscure.
units.literal: whether root or branch, earlier or later, nothing was left unclear.

units.zh: 使誦其說者，如出乎其時；
units.en: So that those who read their account might feel as though they had stepped out of that very age;
units.literal: so that those who recited their account might feel as if they had stepped forth from that very age;

units.zh: 求其指者，如即乎其人。
units.en: and those who sought their meaning might feel as though they stood face to face with the men themselves.
units.literal: and those who sought their meaning might feel as if they were face to face with the men themselves.

units.zh: 是可不謂明足以周萬事之理，道足以適天下之用，智足以通難知之意，文足以發難顯之情者乎？
units.en: Can this not be called clarity that encompasses all principles, a Way that serves the world's needs, wisdom that penetrates what is hard to know, and prose that expresses what is hard to make plain?
units.literal: Can this not be called clarity sufficient to encompass all principles, a Way sufficient to serve the world's needs, wisdom sufficient to penetrate what is hard to know, and style sufficient to express what is hard to reveal?

units.zh: 則方是之時，豈特任政者皆天下之士哉？
units.en: At the time when such texts existed, was it only those who held office who ranked among the talented men of the realm?
units.literal: Then at the time when these texts existed, was it only those charged with government who were men of talent under Heaven?

units.zh: 蓋執簡操筆而隨者，亦皆聖人之徒也。
units.en: Even those who took up the brush and followed in their wake were disciples of the sages.
units.literal: Roughly speaking, even those who took up bamboo strips and wielded the brush in their wake were all disciples of the sages.

units.zh: 兩漢以來爲史者，去之遠矣。
units.en: Historians since the Two Han have fallen far short of this standard.
units.literal: Since the Two Han dynasties, those who wrote histories have stood far from this standard.

units.zh: 司馬遷從五帝三王旣歿數千載之後，秦火之餘，因散絕殘脫之經，以及傳記百家之說，區區掇拾，以集著其善惡之迹，興廢之端，又創己意以爲本紀、世家、八書、列傳之文，斯亦可謂奇矣。
units.en: Sima Qian, thousands of years after the Five Emperors and Three Kings had died and in the wreckage left by the Qin burning of the books, pieced together what survived of broken classics and the writings of the hundred schools, gathered bit by bit the traces of good and evil and the beginnings of rise and fall, and then invented his own structure of Annals, Hereditary Houses, Eight Treatises, and Biographies—this was indeed a marvel.
units.literal: Sima Qian, thousands of years after the Five Emperors and Three Kings had passed away and in the aftermath of the Qin burning, relying on scattered and broken classics and on the reports and traditions of the hundred schools, gathered them bit by bit to compile records of good and evil deeds and the beginnings of rise and fall, and further devised his own scheme for the Annals, Hereditary Houses, Eight Treatises, and Biographies—this may indeed be called remarkable.

units.zh: 然而蔽害天下之聖法，是非顛倒而採摭謬亂者，亦豈少哉！
units.en: Yet how often did he obscure the sage laws of the realm, invert right and wrong, and gather up what was mistaken and confused!
units.literal: Yet how many things did he obscure and harm of the sage laws of the world, how many right and wrong judgments did he overturn in gathering and selecting what was mistaken and confused!

units.zh: 是豈可不謂明不足以周萬事之理，道不足以適天下之用，智不足以通難知之意，文不足以發難顯之情者乎？
units.en: Can he not be said to lack clarity enough to encompass all principles, a Way enough to serve the world's needs, wisdom enough to penetrate what is hard to know, and prose enough to express what is hard to make plain?
units.literal: Can this not be said to be clarity insufficient to encompass all principles, a Way insufficient to serve the world's needs, wisdom insufficient to penetrate what is hard to know, and style insufficient to express what is hard to reveal?

units.zh: 夫自三代以後爲史者如遷之文，亦不可不謂儁偉拔出之材、非常之士也，然顧以謂明不足以周萬事之理，道不足以適天下之用，智不足以通難知之意，文不足以發難顯之情者，何哉？
units.en: Among historians after the Three Dynasties, a writer like Qian must be called a towering talent and an extraordinary man—yet why say that his clarity, Way, wisdom, and prose still fall short?
units.literal: Among historians after the Three Dynasties, for work like Qian's one must call him a towering talent and extraordinary man—yet why should one say that his clarity, Way, wisdom, and style fall short of the standard just named?

units.zh: 蓋聖賢之高致，遷固有不能純達其情而見之於後者矣，故不得而與之也。
units.en: The lofty reach of the sages and worthies—Qian could not wholly convey their inner truth and set it before posterity; therefore he cannot be ranked with the finest historians of antiquity.
units.literal: It is that the lofty reach of sages and worthies—Qian inherently could not fully convey their sentiments and present them to posterity, and so could not be classed with them.

units.zh: 遷之得失如此，況其他邪？
units.en: If Qian's strengths and failings were such, what of the rest?
units.literal: If Qian's merits and faults were such, how much more so others?

units.zh: 至於宋、齊、梁、陳、後魏、後周之書，蓋無以議爲也。
units.en: As for the histories of Song, Qi, Liang, Chen, Later Wei, and Later Zhou, there is scarcely anything worth discussing at all.
units.literal: As for the books of Song, Qi, Liang, Chen, Later Wei, and Later Zhou, there is scarcely anything worth discussing.

units.zh: 子顯之於斯文，喜自馳騁，其更改破析刻彫藻繢之變尤多，而其文益下，豈夫材固不可以強而有邪？
units.en: In this work Zixian delighted in riding his own whim; his revisions, splittings, carvings, and ornamental flourishes were especially numerous, yet his prose grew ever weaker—can a talent truly be forced into being?
units.literal: In this writing Zixian delighted in following his own fancy; his alterations, splitting apart, carving, and ornamental elaborations were especially many, yet his prose grew ever poorer—can talent really not be forced into existence?

units.zh: 數世之史旣然，故其事迹曖味，雖有隨世以就功名之君，相與合謀之臣，未有赫然得傾動天下之耳目，播天下之口者也。
units.en: When histories of several generations are like this, their deeds grow dim: even rulers who rode the times to fame and ministers who plotted together fail to stir the eyes and ears of the world or seize the tongues of all under Heaven.
units.literal: When histories of several generations are thus, their deeds grow dim: even among rulers who rode with the times to win fame and ministers who plotted together, none could plainly stir the eyes and ears of the world and claim the mouths of the world.

units.zh: 而一時偷奪傾危悖理反義之人，亦幸而不暴著於世，豈非所託不得其人故邪？
units.en: Meanwhile men of the age who stole power, overturned states, and defied reason and righteousness also escape exposure—is this not because they did not find the right historian to carry their record?
units.literal: Yet men of that time who stole thrones, overturned states, defied reason and righteousness also fortunately failed to be exposed to the world—is this not because they did not find the right historian as medium?

units.zh: 可不惜哉！
units.en: How lamentable!
units.literal: Is this not lamentable!

units.zh: 蓋史者所以明夫治天下之道也，故爲之者亦必天下之材，然後其任可得而稱也。
units.en: History exists to clarify the Way of governing the realm; its author must therefore be a man of talent fit for the world, and only then can the charge be said to have been met.
units.literal: For history is what clarifies the Way of governing the world; therefore its author must likewise be a man of talent under Heaven, and only then can the task be held to have been fulfilled.

units.zh: 豈可忽哉！
units.en: How could one neglect this!
units.literal: How could one neglect this!

units.zh: 豈可忽哉！
units.en: How could one neglect this!
units.literal: How could one neglect this!

units.zh: 臣恂、臣寶臣、臣穆、臣藻、臣洙、臣覺、臣彥若、臣鞏謹敘目錄昧死上。
units.en: Your subjects Xun, Baochen, Mu, Zao, Zhu, Jue, Yanruo, and Gong respectfully present this catalogue and submit it at the risk of our lives.
units.literal: Your subjects Xun, Baochen, Mu, Zao, Zhu, Jue, Yanruo, and Gong respectfully present this catalogue and report it at the risk of death.

units.zh: 沖母，梁武帝妹新安穆公主，卒於齊世，武帝以沖偏孤，深所鍾愛。
units.en: Chong's mother was Princess Xin'an Mu, a sister of Emperor Wu of Liang. She died in Qi times, and the emperor, seeing that Chong had been left partially orphaned, doted on him.
units.literal: Chong's mother was Princess Xin'an Mu, sister of Emperor Wu of Liang; she died in Qi times, and the Emperor, because Chong was a lone orphan, cherished him deeply.

units.zh: 按梁武帝即位後，追尊其父為文皇帝。
units.en: After Liang Wudi's accession he honored his father posthumously as Emperor Wen.
units.literal: According to the note, after Emperor Wu of Liang took the throne he posthumously honored his father as Emperor Wen.

units.zh: 王沖傳言其母為梁武帝妹新安穆公主，與此合。
units.en: Wang Chong's biography says his mother was Liang Wudi's sister Princess Xin'an Mu, which matches.
units.literal: The biography of Wang Chong says his mother was Emperor Wu of Liang's sister, Princess Xin'an Mu—this agrees.

units.zh: 王沖 王通弟勱 袁敬兄子樞
units.en: Wang Chong; Wang Tong, younger brother Mo; Yuan Jing, nephew Shu
units.literal: Wang Chong; Wang Tong, younger brother Mo; Yuan Jing, nephew Shu

units.zh: [2]琳，齊代娶梁武帝妹義興長公主，有子九人，嵭知名。
units.en: Lin, in Qi times, married Emperor Wu of Liang's sister, Princess of Yixing long; he had nine sons, all of whom won notice.
units.literal: Lin, in Qi times married Emperor Wu of Liang's sister Princess of Yixing long, had nine sons, and all became renowned.

units.zh: 大同末，梁武帝謁園陵，道出朱方，勱隨例迎候，队勱令從輦側，所經山川，莫不顧問，勱隨事應對，咸有故實。
units.en: Near the end of Datong, Emperor Wu of Liang visited the imperial tombs by way of Zhufang; Mo met him as custom required. The emperor ordered Mo to ride beside the carriage; at every hill and stream he asked questions, and Mo answered each with historical precedent.
units.literal: Near the end of Datong, Emperor Wu of Liang visited the imperial tombs; the route passed through Zhufang; Mo greeted him per custom; the Emperor ordered Mo to ride beside the carriage; every mountain and river passed, the Emperor inquired; Mo answered each matter with historical precedent.

units.zh: 漢則馬遷、蕭望，晉則裴楷、張華。
units.en: In Han there were Sima Qian and Xiao Wangzhi; in Jin there were Pei Kai and Zhang Hua.
units.literal: In Han there were Sima Qian and Xiao Wangzhi; in Jin there were Pei Kai and Zhang Hua.

units.zh: 八歲，讀沈約集，見回文研銘，從典援筆擬之，便有佳致。
units.en: At eight he read Shen Yue's collected works. Seeing a palindrome study inscription, Congdian took up the brush to match it and at once produced something fine.
units.literal: At eight he read Shen Yue's collected works; seeing a palindrome study inscription, Congdian took up the brush and imitated it, and at once achieved fine effect.

units.zh: 伏願陛下哀忠念舊，愛孤恤寡，矜愚嘉善，舍過記功，敦骨肉之情，廣寬仁之路，思堯、舜之風，慕禹、湯之德，克己復禮，以成美化，天下幸甚。」
units.en: I venture to hope Your Majesty will pity the loyal and remember the old, cherish the orphaned and comfort the widowed, pity the foolish and praise the good, pardon faults and record merit, thicken kinship among flesh and bone, broaden the path of generous forbearance, think of the manner of Yao and Shun, admire the virtue of Yu and Tang, restrain yourself and return to ritual to complete a transformation of culture — all under Heaven would be greatly blessed."
units.literal: I venture to hope Your Majesty will pity the loyal and remember the old, cherish the orphaned and comfort the widowed, pity the foolish and praise the good, pardon faults and record merit, thicken kinship among flesh and bone, broaden the path of generous forbearance, think of the manner of Yao and Shun, admire the virtue of Yu and Tang, restrain yourself and return to ritual, to complete a transformation of culture — all under Heaven would be greatly blessed."

units.zh: 放勛、重華之世，咸無意於受終，當塗、典午之君，雖有心於揖讓，皆以英才處萬乘，高勳御四海，故能大庇黔首，光宅區縣。
units.en: Yao and Shun took the throne without seeking it; the rulers of Wei and Jin, though they spoke of abdication, still set men of rare talent upon the throne and men of towering merit at the helm of the realm—thus they sheltered the people and brought order to the land.
units.literal: In the ages of Fangxun and Chonghua, both were without intent to receive the end; the lords of Dangtu and Dianwu, though they had mind for yielding, all alike placed men of outstanding talent upon the ten-thousand chariots, with high merit steering the four seas—therefore they could greatly shelter the black-haired people and brightly settle the districts and counties.

units.zh: 既而煙雲表色，日月呈瑞，緯聚東井，龍見譙邦，除舊布新，既彰玄象，遷虞事夏，且協謳訟，[2]九域八荒，同布衷款，百神群祀，皆有誠願。
units.en: Then clouds and mist took auspicious hues; sun and moon showed signs; stars clustered at the Eastern Well; a dragon was seen in Qiao. The old order gave way to the new, and Heaven's signs were plain; as in the transfer from Shun to Yu, the people's acclaim agreed. [2] Within the nine provinces and beyond the eight directions, loyal petitions poured in; every spirit and rite was offered in earnest devotion.
units.literal: Thereafter clouds and mist showed color; sun and moon presented omens; constellations gathered at the Eastern Well; a dragon appeared in the Qiao region. Removing the old and spreading the new, the dark signs were already manifest; shifting from Yu and serving Xia, and moreover matching the songs of praise, [2] the nine domains and eight wilds alike spread forth sincere petitions; the hundred spirits and assembled sacrifices all had sincere wish.

units.zh: 梁氏以天祿斯改，期運永終，欽若唐、虞，推其鼎玉，朕東西退讓，拜手陳辭，避舜子於箕山之陽，求支伯於滄洲之野，而公卿敦逼，率土翹惶，天命難稽，遂享嘉祚。
units.en: The House of Liang, its mandate spent, its turn complete—like Tang and Yu they offered up the regalia. We yielded east and west, bowed with joined hands and pleaded our case, hiding like Shun's son on Mount Ji's sunny slope, seeking Zhibo on Cangzhou's wilds—but ministers pressed us and the realm looked up in dread. Heaven's mandate would not wait; thus We received the glorious throne.
units.literal: The House of Liang, its heavenly blessing now changed, its allotted span ended forever—reverently in accord with Tang and Yu, they pushed forth their tripod and jade. We yielded east and west, bowed with joined hands and spoke our plea, avoiding Shun's son on the sunny slope of Mount Ji, seeking Zhibo on the wilds of Cangzhou—but the dukes and ministers pressed urgently; the whole land looked up in alarm. Heaven's mandate could not be delayed; thus We received the fine fortune.

units.zh: 蕭子恪 弟子範 子顯 子雲
units.en: Xiao Zike; his younger brother Zifan; Xiao Zixian; Xiao Ziyun
units.literal: Xiao Zike; his younger brother Zifan; Zixian; Ziyun

units.zh: 子恪與弟子範等，嘗因事入謝，高祖在文德殿引見之，從容謂曰：「我欲與卿兄弟有言。
units.en: Zike and his younger brother Zifan and the others once came to court to offer thanks on official business. Emperor Wu received them in the Wende Hall and said at his ease, "I wish to speak with you brothers.
units.literal: Zike and his younger brother Zifan and others once entered to give thanks on an affair; the High Ancestor received them in the Wende Hall and said at ease, "I wish to have words with you brothers.

units.zh: 蕭子恪，字景沖，蘭陵人，齊豫章文獻王嶷第二子也。
units.en: Xiao Zike, styled Jingchong, came from Lanling and was the second son of Yi, Prince Wenxian of Yuzhang under Qi.
units.literal: Xiao Zike, styled Jingchong, came from Lanling and was the second son of Yi, Prince Wenxian of Yuzhang under Qi.

units.zh: 卿是宗室，情義異佗，方坦然相期，卿無復懷自外之意。
units.en: You are of the imperial clan; your bond differs from others. I openly expect much of you—do not harbor thoughts of standing apart.
units.literal: You are of the imperial clan; your bond differs from others. I openly expect much of you; do not harbor thoughts of standing apart.

units.zh: 江淹 任昉
units.en: Jiang Yan; Ren Fang
units.literal: Jiang Yan; Ren Fang

units.zh: 江淹，字文通，濟陽考城人也。
units.en: Jiang Yan, styled Wentong, came from Kaocheng in Jiyang.
units.literal: Jiang Yan, styled Wentong, was a native of Kaocheng in Jiyang.

units.zh: 諡曰憲伯。
units.en: His posthumous title was Xianbo.
units.literal: His posthumous title was Xianbo.

units.zh: 天監元年，爲散騎常侍、左衛將軍，封臨沮縣開國伯，食邑四百戶。
units.en: In Tianjian 1, he became Regular Attendant and Left Guard General, and was enfeoffed as founding Count of Linju county with a fief of four hundred households.
units.literal: In Tianjian 1, he became Regular Attendant and Left Guard General, and was enfeoffed as founding Count of Linju county with a fief of four hundred households.

units.zh: 其年，以疾遷金紫光祿大夫，改封醴陵侯。
units.en: That year, because of illness, he was transferred to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon, and his fief was changed to Marquis of Liling.
units.literal: That year, because of illness, he was transferred to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon, and his fief was changed to Marquis of Liling.

units.zh: 起家南徐州從事，轉奉朝請。
units.en: He began as a South Xuzhou staff officer, then became a court attendant.
units.literal: He first entered office as staff officer in South Xuzhou, then was transferred to attendant at court.

units.zh: 淹少以文章顯，晚節才思微退，時人皆謂之才盡。
units.en: He had risen on his pen, yet in old age his gift thinned; men said his talent was spent.
units.literal: Yan had been famed early for writing; in his late years his talent waned—the age said his talent was spent.

units.zh: 凡所著述百餘篇，自撰爲前後集，幷《齊史》十志，並行於世。
units.en: He left more than a hundred works, front and rear collections of his own, and the Ten Annals of Qi—all still in the world.
units.literal: All his writings exceeded a hundred pieces; he compiled front and rear collections himself, together with the Ten Annals of Qi History, all circulating in the world.

units.zh: 景素與腹心日夜謀議，淹知禍機將發，乃贈詩十五首以諷焉。
units.en: Jingsu and his inner circle schemed night and day; Yan saw disaster near and offered fifteen poems as warning.
units.literal: Jingsu and his intimates plotted day and night; Yan saw ruin coming and sent fifteen poems as indirect warning.

units.zh: 建元初，又爲驃騎豫章王記室，帶東武令，參掌詔册，並典國史。
units.en: At Jianyuan's opening he was again valiant-cavalry record-keeper to the Prince of Yuzhang, magistrate of Dongwu in addition, drafting edicts and patents and tending the national history.
units.literal: At the start of Jianyuan he was again valiant-cavalry record-keeper to the Prince of Yuzhang, with concurrent magistrate of Dongwu, charged with edicts and patents and also keeper of the national history.

units.zh: 少孤貧好學，沉靜少交遊。
units.en: Left fatherless while young, poor but devoted to books, he lived inwardly and made few friends.
units.literal: Orphaned young, poor, and fond of study, he was quiet and kept few companions.

units.zh: 宋建平王景素好士，淹隨景素在南兗州。
units.en: Jingsu, Prince of Jianping under Song, prized men of letters; Yan served him in Southern Yanzhou.
units.literal: Jingsu, Prince of Jianping under Song, loved scholars; Yan followed Jingsu in Southern Yanzhou.

units.zh: 昇明初，齊帝輔政，聞其才，召爲尚書駕部郎、驃騎參軍事。
units.en: At the start of Ascendant Bright, with Qi's emperor as regent, he heard of Yan and made him secretariat director of the imperial equipage and valiant-cavalry staff officer.
units.literal: At the start of the Ascendant Bright era, when Qi's emperor held regency, he heard of Yan's talent and summoned him as Masters of Writing director of the imperial equipage and valiant-cavalry staff officer.

units.zh: 廣陵令郭彥文得罪，辭連淹，繫州獄。
units.en: Guangling magistrate Guo Yanwen ran afoul of the law; Yan was caught up in the case and held in the provincial prison.
units.literal: Guangling magistrate Guo Yanwen offended the law; Yan was implicated in his defense and imprisoned in the provincial jail.

units.zh: 淹獄中上書曰：
units.en: From his cell Yan sent up a memorial, which said:
units.literal: In prison Yan submitted a memorial that read:

units.zh: 昔者，賤臣叩心，飛霜擊於燕地；
units.en: Long ago a loyal subject struck his heart in anguish, and frost answered on the plains of Yan;
units.literal: Of old a loyal minister beat his breast in grief until frost fell on the land of Yan;

units.zh: 庶女告天，振風襲於齊臺。
units.en: a common daughter cried to Heaven, and a rending wind struck the tower of Qi.
units.literal: a common woman cried to Heaven until a shaking wind struck the tower of Qi.

units.zh: 下官每讀其書，未嘗不廢卷流涕。
units.en: Whenever your servant reads those lines he cannot close the book without tears.
units.literal: Each time your servant reads those words he cannot lay the scroll down without weeping.

units.zh: 何者？
units.en: Why is that?
units.literal: Why?

units.zh: 士有一定之論，女有不易之行。
units.en: A gentleman holds to a fixed standard; a woman keeps faith that will not bend.
units.literal: A gentleman has a settled code; a woman has conduct that does not change.

units.zh: 信而見疑，貞而爲戮，是以壯夫義士伏死而不顧者此也。
units.en: Believed in yet doubted, steadfast yet slain—for that reason stalwarts and men of honor face death and never turn aside.
units.literal: Trusted yet suspected, loyal yet punished to death—therefore brave men and men of honor lie down to die and do not look back.

units.zh: 下官聞仁不可恃，善不可依，始謂徒語，乃今知之。
units.en: Your servant heard that kindness cannot be trusted and virtue cannot be depended on; he took it for empty saying—now he knows it true.
units.literal: Your servant has heard that benevolence cannot be relied on and goodness cannot be leaned on; he once thought that mere talk, but now he knows it.

units.zh: 伏願大王暫停左右，少加憐鑒。
units.en: He bows and begs Your Highness to stay your attendants briefly and lend a measure of pity and clear judgment.
units.literal: He bows and begs Your Highness to pause your attendants a moment and grant a little pity and clear sight.

units.zh: 下官本蓬戶桑樞之民，布衣韋帶之士，退不飾《詩書》以驚愚，進不買名聲於天下。
units.en: Your servant is a man of wicker doors and mulberry pivots, a common scholar in hemp and leather; he did not dress up the Odes and Documents to dazzle fools, nor purchase renown under heaven.
units.literal: Your servant was born a man of wicker doors and mulberry pivots, a scholar in hemp cloak and leather belt; in retreat he did not polish the Odes and Documents to startle the dull, in advance he did not buy a name in the world.

units.zh: 日者謬得升降承明之闕，出入金華之殿，何嘗不局影凝嚴，側身扃禁者乎？
units.en: Not long ago, by error, he passed the Bright Hall gate and walked the Golden Flower halls—was he not always folding his shadow before the guards and edging past the locks?
units.literal: Lately, by mistake, he was raised and lowered through the gate of Bright Hall, in and out of the Golden Flower Hall—when did he not shrink his shadow before stern guards and walk sideways past barred doors?

units.zh: 竊慕大王之義，爲門下之賓，備鳴盜淺術之餘，豫三五賤伎之末。
units.en: He secretly honored Your Highness's righteousness and entered your gate as a retainer, given only the dregs of shallow craft and a place among the meanest talents.
units.literal: He secretly admired Your Highness's righteousness and became a guest at your gate, supplied with the leavings of shallow arts and placed among the humblest of petty skills.

units.zh: 大王惠以恩光，眄以顏色。
units.en: Your Highness favored him with grace and looked on him with kindness.
units.literal: Your Highness showed him favor in grace and glanced on him with a kind face.

units.zh: 實佩荊卿黃金之賜，竊感豫讓國士之分矣。
units.en: He truly bore the gift of Jing Ke's gold and felt in his bones the debt Yu Rang owed a lord of the land.
units.literal: Truly he wore the gift of Jing Ke's yellow gold and felt in secret the bond Yu Rang owed a lord of the realm.

units.zh: 常欲結纓伏劍，少謝萬一，剖心摩踵，以報所天。
units.en: He often meant to knot his cap and offer his sword, to repay you in the least part, to break his heart and grind his heels for the lord he served.
units.literal: He often wished to knot his cap and lay down his sword, to repay you in the smallest measure, to split his heart and wear down his heels for the lord he served.

units.zh: 不圖小人固陋，坐貽謗缺，迹墜昭憲，身限幽圄。
units.en: He never dreamed a petty man's spite would trap him in accusation; his name fell from the bright statutes, his body was caged in the black jail.
units.literal: He never thought a mean man's narrowness would seat him in slander; his steps fell from bright law, his person was shut in a dark cell.

units.zh: 履影弔心，酸鼻痛骨。
units.en: He treads on his shadow and weeps in his heart; acid rises in his nose and pain cuts his bones.
units.literal: He walks his shadow and mourns his heart; his nose burns sour and his bones ache.

units.zh: 下官聞虧名爲辱，虧形次之，是以每一念來，忽若有遺。
units.en: Your servant has heard that to lose one's name is shame and to lose one's body is worse still; each time the thought returns he feels something torn away.
units.literal: Your servant has heard that to lose one's name is disgrace and to lose one's form comes next; therefore each time the thought returns he feels as though something were lost.

units.zh: 加以涉旬月，迫季秋，天光沉陰，左右無色。
units.en: Moreover a month has passed into late autumn; heaven hangs dark and there is no light at either hand.
units.literal: Moreover he has passed a full month and reached late autumn; the sky sinks in gloom and there is no color left at his sides.

units.zh: 身非木石，與獄吏爲伍。
units.en: He is not wood or stone, yet he keeps company with the turnkeys.
units.literal: His person is not wood or stone, yet he shares a ward with the jailers.

units.zh: 此少卿所以仰天搥心，泣盡而繼之以血者也。
units.en: That is why Sir Shaoqing beat his breast to Heaven, wept his eyes dry, and still shed blood.
units.literal: That is why Sir Shaoqing beat his breast to Heaven, wept until he had no tears, and went on bleeding.

units.zh: 下官雖乏鄉曲之譽，然嘗聞君子之行矣。
units.en: Your servant lacks fame in his district, yet he has heard the gentleman's way.
units.literal: Your servant lacks the praise of his village, yet he has heard how a gentleman walks.

units.zh: 其上則隱於簾肆之間，臥於巖石之下；
units.en: At the highest he hides behind shop curtains or sleeps on mountain stone;
units.literal: At the highest he hides between curtain and market stall or lies on stone in the hills;

units.zh: 次則結綬金馬之庭，高議雲臺之上；
units.en: next he ties his sash in the hall of golden horses and argues great policy on the Cloud Terrace;
units.literal: next he knots his sash in the court of golden horses and speaks high doctrine on the Cloud Terrace;

units.zh: 次則虜南越之君，繫單于之頸：俱啓丹册，並圖青史。
units.en: next he seizes the lord of Southern Yue and collars the Chanyu: each enters the vermilion book and wins a line in the blue annals.
units.literal: next he takes the lord of Southern Yue captive and binds the Chanyu by the neck: all open the red register and share a place in the green histories.

units.zh: 寧當爭分寸之末，競刀錐之利哉！
units.en: Would he fight for a hair's breadth or compete for a needle's point!
units.literal: Would he contend for a hair's breadth or vie for the edge of a knife awl!

units.zh: 然下官聞積毀銷金，積讒糜骨。
units.en: Yet your servant has heard that slander heaped high can melt gold and malice heaped high can grind bone to dust.
units.literal: Yet your servant has heard that slander piled high melts gold and calumny piled high grinds bone to meal.

units.zh: 古則直生取疑於盜金，近則伯魚被名於不義。
units.en: In antiquity Straightborn was doubted over stolen gold; in recent times Boyu was marked with an unjust name.
units.literal: In antiquity Straightborn was suspected for stolen gold; in recent times Boyu was stained with an unrighteous name.

units.zh: 彼之二才，猶或如此；
units.en: Men of such gifts suffered thus;
units.literal: Those two talents were treated so;

units.zh: 況在下官，焉能自免。
units.en: how much more your servant—how could he be spared!
units.literal: how much more your servant—how could he escape!

units.zh: 昔上將之恥，絳侯幽獄；
units.en: Of old a great general's shame was Jiang Hou in the cells;
units.literal: Of old a great general's shame was Jiang Hou in a dungeon;

units.zh: 名臣之羞，史遷下室，如下官尚何言哉！
units.en: a famous minister's blush was the Historian in the pit—as for your servant, what words remain!
units.literal: a famous minister's blush was the Historian in the lower chamber—as for your servant, what more can he say!

units.zh: 夫魯連之智，辭祿而不反；
units.en: Lu Zhonglian had wisdom yet refused rank and never came back;
units.literal: Lu Zhonglian was wise yet declined salary and never returned;

units.zh: 接輿之賢，行歌而忘歸。
units.en: Jieyu had worth yet sang as he walked and forgot the homeward road.
units.literal: Jieyu was worthy yet walked singing and forgot to go home.

units.zh: 子陵閉關於東越，仲蔚杜門於西秦，亦良可知也。
units.en: Yan Ziling closed his door in Eastern Yue and Zhong Wei sealed his gate in Western Qin—the meaning is clear enough.
units.literal: Yan Ziling shut his gate in Eastern Yue and Zhong Wei barred his door in Western Qin—the lesson is plain enough.

units.zh: 若使下官事非其虛，罪得其實，亦當鉗口吞舌，伏匕首以殞身，何以見齊魯奇節之人，燕趙悲歌之士乎？
units.en: If your servant's charge were true and his guilt solid, he should seal his mouth, swallow his tongue, and die on a blade—why meet the strange honor of Qi and Lu or the mourning singers of Yan and Zhao!
units.literal: If your servant's affair were not empty and his guilt were real, he should clamp his mouth, swallow his tongue, and fall on a dagger—why should he face the strange integrity of Qi and Lu or the grieving singers of Yan and Zhao!

units.zh: 方今聖曆欽明，天下樂業，青雲浮雒，榮光塞河。
units.en: Now the sacred reign is revered and bright; all under heaven delights in its labor; azure clouds drift above the Luo, splendor blocks the river.
units.literal: Now the holy calendar is revered and bright; the realm rejoices in its work; azure clouds float over the Luo, glory fills the river.

units.zh: 西洎臨洮、狄道，北距飛狐、陽原，莫不浸仁沐義，照景飲醴。
units.en: West to Lintao and Didao, north to Flying Fox and Yangyuan—every land is steeped in kindness, washed in duty, lit by the sun, drinking the sweet cup.
units.literal: West to Lintao and Didao, north to Flying Fox and Yangyuan—none but is steeped in benevolence, bathed in righteousness, warmed by the sun, drinking the sweet wine.

units.zh: 而下官抱痛圜門，含憤獄戶，一物之微，有足悲者。
units.en: Yet your servant nurses pain at the round gate and hoards rage in the jail— the smallest matter is cause for grief.
units.literal: Yet your servant embraces pain at the round gate and holds wrath in the prison door; the slightest thing is enough to grieve.

units.zh: 仰惟大王少垂明白，則梧丘之魂，不愧於沉首；
units.en: He looks up and begs Your Highness to grant a little clear sight; then the shade at Wuzhu Mound need not blush for a buried head;
units.literal: He looks up and begs Your Highness to bend a little clear light; then the soul at Wuzhu Mound need not blush for a head sunk in earth;

units.zh: 鵠亭之鬼，無恨於灰骨。
units.en: the ghost at Goose Pavilion need not regret bones burned to ash.
units.literal: the ghost at Goose Pavilion need not regret bones turned to ash.

units.zh: 不任肝膽之切，敬因執事以聞。
units.en: Unable to bear the cut of heart and liver, he respectfully reports through your officers.
units.literal: Unable to bear the cut of liver and gall, he respectfully sends word through your attendants.

units.zh: 此心旣照，死且不朽。
units.en: Once this heart is known, even death will not die.
units.literal: Once this heart is seen, death itself will not perish.

units.zh: 景素覽書，卽日出之。
units.en: Jingsu read the letter and freed him the same day.
units.literal: Jingsu read the memorial and released him that same day.

units.zh: 景素爲荊州，淹從之鎮。
units.en: When Jingsu took Jing province, Yan went with him to the command.
units.literal: When Jingsu went to Jing province, Yan followed him to the post.

units.zh: 淹每從容諫曰：「流言納禍，二叔所以同亡；
units.en: Yan often urged him gently: "Rumor draws ruin—
units.literal: Yan often remonstrated at leisure: "Slander brings disaster in—

units.zh: 殿下不求宗廟之安，而信左右之計，則復見麋鹿霜露棲於姑蘇之臺矣。」
units.en: that is how the Seven States were destroyed. Your Highness does not seek the altars' safety but trusts men at your ear; then you will again see deer in frost and dew on the Terrace of Gusu."
units.literal: that is why the Seven States all fell. Your Highness does not seek the peace of the ancestral temples but trusts the counsel of those at your side; then you will again see deer in frost and dew lodging on the Terrace of Gusu."

units.zh: 景素不納。
units.en: Jingsu would not listen.
units.literal: Jingsu did not accept his advice.

units.zh: 淹固求之，景素大怒，言於選部，黜爲建安吳興令。
units.en: Yan insisted; Jingsu raged, spoke to personnel, and demoted him to Jian'an magistrate in Wu-xing.
units.literal: Yan pressed his claim; Jingsu was furious and spoke to the selection office, demoting him to magistrate of Jian'an in Wu-xing.

units.zh: 淹對曰：「昔項強而劉弱，袁衆而曹寡，羽號令諸侯，卒受一劍之辱，紹跨躡四州，終爲奔北之虜。
units.en: Yan answered, "Once Xiang Yu was strong and Liu Bang weak, Yuan Shao had numbers and Cao Cao few; Yu ruled the lords yet died by one sword, Yuan held four provinces yet fled north in defeat.
units.literal: Yan answered, "Of old Xiang was strong and Liu weak, Yuan had many men and Cao few; Yu commanded the feudal lords yet in the end suffered the shame of a single sword, Yuan straddled four provinces yet ended a fugitive north of the river.

units.zh: 淹曰：「公雄武有奇略，一勝也；
units.en: Yan said, "You are boldly martial with a singular plan—first victory;
units.literal: Yan said, "Your Lordship is boldly martial with a strange design—one victory;

units.zh: 故雖豺狼十萬，而終爲我獲焉。」
units.en: Though jackals number in the tens of thousands, in the end they are yours."
units.literal: Though they have a hundred thousand wolves, in the end they will be ours."

units.zh: 永明初，遷驍騎將軍，掌國史。
units.en: At Yongming's opening he became valiant cavalry general and still held the national history.
units.literal: At the start of Yongming he was made Valiant Cavalry General and kept charge of the national history.

units.zh: 少帝初，以本官兼御史中丞。
units.en: When the Depraved Emperor began his reign Yan kept his rank and also served as censor.
units.literal: At the start of the Depraved Emperor's reign he held his former post with concurrent Censor.

units.zh: 於是彈中書令謝朏，司徒左長史王繢、護軍長史庾弘遠，並以久疾不預山陵公事；
units.en: He then impeached secretariat director Xie Fei, minister of education left chief of staff Wang Ji, and protecting-army chief clerk Yu Hongyuan—for long illness and absence from the imperial tomb rites;
units.literal: Thereupon he impeached Secretariat Director Xie Fei, Left Chief of Staff to the Minister of Education Wang Ji, and Protecting Army Chief Clerk Yu Hongyuan—all for long illness and failure to attend the mountain tomb rites;

units.zh: 明帝謂淹曰：「宋世以來，不復有嚴明中丞，君今日可謂近世獨步。」
units.en: Mingdi told Yan, "Since the Song there has been no censor this stern; you may be called alone in our age."
units.literal: Mingdi said to Yan, "Since Song times there has been no stern censor like you; today you may be called unmatched in recent generations."

units.zh: 永元中，崔慧景舉兵圍京城，衣冠悉投名刺，淹稱疾不往。
units.en: In Yongyuan, Cui Huijing besieged the capital; every gentleman sent his card, but Yan pleaded sickness and stayed away.
units.literal: In Yongyuan, Cui Huijing raised troops and besieged the capital; officials all sent calling cards—Yan claimed illness and did not go.

units.zh: 東昏末，淹以秘書監兼衛尉，固辭不獲免，遂親職。
units.en: At the end of Donghun's reign, Yan, as Palace Library Director, was also made Commandant of the Guards. He firmly declined but could not be excused, and so took up the office himself.
units.literal: At the end of Donghun's reign, Yan, as Palace Library Director, was also made Commandant of the Guards. He firmly declined but could not be excused, and so took up the office himself.

units.zh: 中興元年，遷吏部尚書。
units.en: In Zhongxing 1, he was transferred to Minister of Personnel.
units.literal: In Zhongxing 1, he was transferred to Minister of Personnel.

units.zh: 淹乃謂子弟曰：「吾本素宦，不求富貴，今之忝竊，遂至於此。
units.en: Yan then told his sons and younger kinsmen, "I was originally a plain official and did not seek wealth or rank. Now, through undeserved favor, I have reached this point.
units.literal: Yan then told his sons and younger kinsmen, "I was originally a plain official and did not seek wealth or rank. Now, through undeserved favor, I have reached this point.

units.zh: 吾功名旣立，正欲歸身草萊耳。」
units.en: Now that my achievements and name are established, I simply wish to return myself to the fields."
units.literal: Now that my achievements and name are established, I simply wish to return myself to the fields."

units.zh: 四年卒，時年六十二。
units.en: He died in the fourth year, aged sixty-two.
units.literal: He died in the fourth year, aged sixty-two.

units.zh: 子蒍襲封嗣，自丹陽尹丞爲長城令，有罪削爵。
units.en: His son Wei took the title, rose from Danyang aide to magistrate of Changcheng, then lost the fief for a crime.
units.literal: His son Wei inherited the fief; from Assistant to the Danyang Intendant he became magistrate of Changcheng; for a crime his noble rank was stripped.

units.zh: 及鎮京口，淹又爲鎮軍參軍事，領南東海郡丞。
units.en: When he held Jingkou, Yan became pacifying-army staff officer and also magistrate of Southern Donghai.
units.literal: When he garrisoned Jingkou, Yan was again made staff officer to the Pacifying Army and concurrently magistrate of Southern Donghai commandery.

units.zh: 會南東海太守陸澄丁艱，淹自謂郡丞應行郡事，景素用司馬柳世隆。
units.en: When Southern Donghai prefect Lu Cheng began mourning, Yan assumed the aide should run the commandery; Jingsu gave the post to staff officer Liu Shilong.
units.literal: When Southern Donghai prefect Lu Cheng entered mourning for his father, Yan thought that as commandery aide he should act as prefect; Jingsu appointed staff officer Liu Shilong instead.

units.zh: 淹在縣三年。
units.en: Yan served in the county three years.
units.literal: Yan held the district three years.

units.zh: 俄而荊州刺史沈攸之作亂，高帝謂淹曰：「天下紛紛若是，君謂何如？」
units.en: Soon Jing inspector Shen Youzhi rose in arms; Gaodi asked Yan, "The world is chaos like this—what is your view?"
units.literal: Before long Jing inspector Shen Youzhi rebelled; Gaodi said to Yan, "The realm is in such turmoil—what do you think?"

units.zh: 是時軍書表記，皆使淹具草。
units.en: In those days every army dispatch and memorial passed through Yan's hand.
units.literal: At that time military reports and memorials were all drafted by Yan.

units.zh: 時明帝作相，因謂淹曰：「君昔在尚書中，非公事不妄行，在官寬猛能折衷；
units.en: Mingdi was regent and told Yan, "In the secretariat you never moved without public business; in office you could balance mercy and severity;
units.literal: Mingdi was then chief minister and said to Yan, "When you were in the Masters of Writing you never acted without public cause; in office you balanced lenity and severity;

units.zh: 淹答曰：「今日之事，可謂當官而行，更恐才劣志薄，不足以仰稱明旨耳。」
units.en: Yan answered, "Today's charge is to act as the post requires; I only fear my gift is small and my resolve thin for your clear command."
units.literal: Yan answered, "Today's task may be called doing the office as it demands; I only fear talent too slight and will too thin to rise to your bright intent."

units.zh: 明帝卽位，爲車騎臨海王長史。
units.en: When Mingdi succeeded, Yan became chief of staff to the valiant-cavalry prince of Linhai.
units.literal: When Mingdi took the throne, Yan was made chief of staff to the Valiant Cavalry Prince of Linhai.

units.zh: 及義師至新林，淹微服來奔，高祖板爲冠軍將軍，秘書監如故，尋兼司徒左長史。
units.en: When the righteous army reached Xinlin, Yan came over in plain clothes. Gaozu provisionally appointed him Champion General, leaving him as Palace Library Director as before, and soon made him concurrently left chief clerk to the Minister over the Masses.
units.literal: When the righteous army reached Xinlin, Yan came over in plain clothes. Gaozu provisionally appointed him Champion General, leaving him as Palace Library Director as before, and soon made him concurrently left chief clerk to the Minister over the Masses.

units.zh: 普通四年，高祖追念淹功，復封蒍吳昌伯，邑如先。
units.en: In Putong year 4 Gaozu remembered Yan's service and made Wei marquis of Wuchang again, with the old fief.
units.literal: In the fourth year of Putong, Gaozu recalled Yan's merit and re-enfeoffed Wei as Marquis of Wuchang, fief as before.
